name: Vector display arcade
summary: The beam of the tube draws lines, not pixels. Bright monochrome or colour outlines glow on pure black, with no fill, no texture and a world built from wire shapes.

philosophy.core_thesis: A world can be drawn with light alone: a few sharp glowing lines on black are enough for the eye to build space.
design_principles: Draw every object as an outline of straight line segments; use no filled area.
Keep the ground pure black; it is the space between the lines.
Make the lines bright and let them bloom by 1–3 px into the dark.
Use 1 to 4 colours of full saturation, one for each class of object.
Show depth with perspective wireframes and a vanishing point, not with shading.
Keep each shape under about 30 segments so it reads at a glance.
anti_patterns: Dense detail that the beam cannot draw in one frame
Pixel steps on a diagonal line

projection_and_camera.camera: Locked, or a slow fly-through down a tube or a grid.
projection_and_camera.framing: The whole field of play on one screen, with the player at the bottom or the centre.

geometry.primitive: A straight line segment between two points on a 1024 by 1024 addressable field; about 1024 by 768 of it is visible.
geometry.budget: A few hundred segments for each frame on the whole screen.
geometry.edge_rule: Perfect straight lines with no steps; the ends of lines glow a little brighter.
geometry.proportion: Abstract: a ship, a rock and a city are all the same order of size.

surface.texture_rule: No texture; a surface is its outline.
surface.filtering: None; the beam draws the line in analogue.
surface.material_model: No material; every line is a light source.

palette.strategy: Light on black: white or one hue on a monochrome tube, up to 7 saturated hues on a colour tube.
palette.colour_depth: 1 to 3 bits: on or off for each colour gun

lighting.shadows: No shadows: a line casts none.
lighting.atmosphere: A soft glow around each line from the phosphor of the tube.

world_and_space.scale: One screen is the whole world; the scale is symbolic.
world_and_space.interiors: A room is a wireframe box in perspective, its edges only.
world_and_space.exteriors: A street is a perspective grid that runs to one vanishing point, with wire buildings at the sides.
world_and_space.threshold: A cut to a new screen.

principles.rule: Put the player shape at the bottom centre or the screen centre; every line leads there.
Show depth with 3 to 6 nested outlines that shrink toward the vanishing point.
Use one light layer only: the lines themselves.

interface.placement: A score in the top corners in the same vector lines, about 5% of the screen.
interface.type_and_icons: Stroke letters built from 5 to 10 segments.
interface.diegesis: None; the score sits on top of the black ground.

emotion.target_response: A cold, exact wonder: the player sees a world made of light lines and fills in the rest.

avoid_when: The brief needs material, texture or warmth.
The scene needs many small objects.

modifiers.how: Fill the shapes with a small flat palette and move to a tile grid.
Keep the perspective; fill the wireframes with flat-shaded polygons.

render_resolution.note: The addressable field of the beam (1024 by 1024), not a raster.

texel_density.note: No texture: the floor of the range.
